# dsh-webchat-anchor-fix

A one-rule fix for a geometry bug in
`@jaychang1989/dsh-webchat`: after
a fullscreen/windowed toggle

the DeepSeek panel can keep the size and position of
the window state it came from, until the guest
is reloaded or reopened.

The upstream package is untouched and keeps tracking its own releases. This is a
separate package th
at styles the DSH web surface's own document.
## The bug

webchat keeps the guest in a fixed-position overlay and copies the panel's box
into it from JavaScri

chat keeps the guest in a fixed-position overlay and copies the panel's box
into it from JavaScript:

- `syncBounds(host)` reads `.dsh-wc-host.getBoundingClientRect()` and writes
inline `left`, `top`, `

itself is never laid out by the shell, so when a fullscreen
transition outruns the copy, the overla
y stays at the old numbers.

Because the copy is a JavaScript step, there is a window in which the panel has
already moved and th

e overlay has not. Nothing in the current design closes that
window; a missed event leaves it open i

s not. Nothing in the current design closes that
window; a missed event leaves it open indefinitely.
## The fix
The copy is removed from the loop. One stylesheet:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The browser resolves those four values on every layout. The overlay follows the
panel through fullsc

reen, windowed, sidebar and resize changes with no
listeners, no timers, no `ResizeObserver` and no
JavaScript after mount.

`!important` is not a shortcut: webchat writes the four properties inline, and an
important author d

eclaration is the only declaration in the cascade that
outranks a normal inline one.

`body:has(.dsh-wc-host)` keeps the geometry rule inert when no panel host exists,
so an overlay left
behind for any reason still gets webchat's own inline values.
## What it touches

- One `<style>` element in the DSH web surface's document.
- Nothing inside the DeepSeek page: the w

ebview is never read, written, or
messaged. No `insertCSS` into the guest, no `executeJavaScript`.
-

No network requests, no cookies, no `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`, no
user-agent changes.
- No la

yout mode, paint or stacking overrides: only the four geometry
properties and the anchor name.

That boundary matters. The panel bug is a DSH-side layout issue; the DeepSeek
page's risk-control co
nversation is not this package's business.
## Contract and failure mode
Two webchat hooks are used, both public-facing:

- the class `.dsh-wc-host` on the panel host div;
- the attribute `[data-dsh-webchat-overlay]` on th
e guest overlay div.

If a future release renames either, the rules stop matching and the overlay
falls back to webchat's

inline geometry — exactly today's behaviour. The fix
goes dormant, it does not break the panel.

`@supports` provides the second failure mode: an engine without CSS anchor
positioning ignores the w

hole block. The client half logs one console warning
so the dormancy is visible.
## Known limit

This aligns the overlay to the panel element that exists. If the panel element
itself is laid out at

the wrong size (a shell-level layout bug rather than a
missed copy), the overlay will faithfully tr

ack the wrong box. In that case the
bug is upstream in the app shell, not in webchat's sync.

inline geometry, th

en moves the layout three ways, resizes the viewport, hides
and shows the overlay, and removes and r

e-creates the host — all without calling
into the package. Every step is measured against the host's

the host — all without calling
into the package. Every step is measured against the host's own rect.

prefix the URL with `h
ttps://gh-proxy.com/`.

**Caution:** install this only if a fullscreen or window toggle actually leaves
the panel at the old

bounds. If the panel behaves, the fix has nothing to
correct. It is independent of any skin and ins
